INCIDENT REPORT from on-call: "Finance says our revenue numbers are higher than what they reconcile to, including for older months. Can you look?"

Investigate. Start by locating the executive revenue KPI in DataHub.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

Can be called again to revise the root cause before a repair passes. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.
tools.name: confirm_root_cause

tools.description: Escalate upstream data that is lost, missing or stale and cannot be recovered exactly. No repair is allowed afterwards. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.

tools.description: Record the incident in DataHub on the affected dataset.
tools.name: write_back

tools.description: End the run with a final report.
tools.name: finish

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:

2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.

     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.

tools.name: write_back

tools.description: End the run with a final report.
tools.name: finish

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

tools.name: run_sql

tools.name: read_transform

tools.name: run_checks

tools.description: Confirm a root cause with cited evidence; use this (then propose_repair) whenever the true values can be reconstructed exactly. Can be called again to revise the root cause before a repair passes. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.
tools.name: confirm_root_cause

tools.description: Escalate upstream data that is lost, missing or stale and cannot be recovered exactly. No repair is allowed afterwards. The asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect originates, not the file you patch. asset: schema-qualified table name (schema.table) or its DataHub URN; field: column name.
tools.name: escalate_upstream

tools.description: Declare no incident, citing a baseline comparison.
tools.name: declare_no_incident

tools.description: Replace one transform's full SQL; the pipeline is rebuilt in a scratch copy and every invariant is checked.
tools.name: propose_repair

tools.description: Record the incident in DataHub on the affected dataset.
tools.name: write_back

tools.description: End the run with a final report.
tools.name: finish

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

input.summary: raw.raw_customers violates its documented "one row per customer" contract: 289 of 2000 customer_ids have two rows each (2289 total rows), with the extra row always stamped created_at=2026-08-01 and often a changed segment (e.g., c00002: enterprise/2025-12-20 vs smb/2026-08-01). staging.stg_customers passes these duplicates through unfiltered, and marts.fct_revenue INNER JOINs stg_customers on customer_id, so every order placed by one of these 289 customers is double-counted. Because fct_revenue is a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, this fans out order_count and revenue_usd for ALL historical days that contain orders from the affected customers (order_count 27101 in fct vs 23709 in stg = +14.3%, matching 289/2000=14.45% of the customer base) — exactly matching finance's observation that revenue is overstated "including for older months." run_checks confirms: fct_order_count_matches_stg fails (27101 vs 23709), revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band fail (~11-17% high every day), and historical_revenue_immutable fails (87 days changed on rebuild).

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

Because fct_revenue is a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, this fans out order_count and revenue_usd for ALL historical days that contain orders from the affected customers (order_count 27101 in fct vs 23709 in stg = +14.3%, matching 289/2000=14.45% of the customer base) — exactly matching finance's observation that revenue is overstated "including for older months." run_checks confirms: fct_order_count_matches_stg fails (27101 vs 23709), revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band fail (~11-17% high every day), and historical_revenue_immutable fails (87 days changed on rebuild).

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

Because fct_revenue is a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, this fans out order_count and revenue_usd for ALL historical days that contain orders from the affected customers (order_count 27101 in fct vs 23709 in stg = +14.3%, matching 289/2000=14.45% of the customer base) — exactly matching finance's observation that revenue is overstated "including for older months." run_checks confirms: fct_order_count_matches_stg fails (27101 vs 23709), revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band fail (~11-17% high every day), and historical_revenue_immutable fails (87 days changed on rebuild).

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

content.text: Now let's implement the minimal repair: dedupe `stg_customers` to enforce one row per customer_id.

input.new_sql:
-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
-- Fix: raw.raw_customers violates its "one row per customer" contract for 289 customer_ids
-- (duplicate rows injected with created_at=2026-08-01). Deduplicate here, keeping the most
-- recent snapshot per customer_id, so downstream joins in marts.fct_revenue do not fan out
-- and double-count orders/revenue for affected customers.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_customers AS
SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    country,
    created_at
FROM (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        segment,
        country,
        CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_at,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM raw.raw_customers
)
WHERE rn = 1;

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
-- Fix: raw.raw_customers violates its "one row per customer" contract for 289 customer_ids
-- (duplicate rows injected with created_at=2026-08-01). Deduplicate here, keeping the most
-- recent snapshot per customer_id, so downstream joins in marts.fct_revenue do not fan out
-- and double-count orders/revenue for affected customers.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_customers AS
SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    country,
    created_at
FROM (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        segment,
        country,
        CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_at,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM raw.raw_customers
)
WHERE rn = 1;

You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

input.summary:
Incident: Executive revenue KPI (marts.exec_metric) overstated revenue and order_count by ~11-17% across all historical days, matching finance's reconciliation complaint.

Root cause: raw.raw_customers (owned by Jordan Lee / Payments Platform team) violates its own documented contract of "one row per customer." 289 of 2000 customer_ids have a duplicate row, each stamped created_at=2026-08-01 and frequently carrying a changed `segment` value (e.g., c00002: enterprise/2025-12-20 vs smb/2026-08-01). staging.stg_customers passed these duplicates through unchanged, and marts.fct_revenue's INNER JOIN to stg_customers on customer_id fanned out orders for those 289 customers, double-counting them. Because fct_revenue does a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, every historical day containing an order from one of the affected customers was inflated on each run - not just recent days - which is why finance saw the discrepancy "including for older months."

Evidence: fct_order_count_matches_stg check failed (27101 vs 23709, +14.3%, consistent with 289/2000=14.45% of customers being duplicated); revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band failed every day by ~11-17%; historical_revenue_immutable flagged 87 changed historical days.

Fix applied (scoped, verified): staging/stg_customers.sql now deduplicates raw.raw_customers by customer_id, keeping the most recent snapshot (MAX created_at) per customer, restoring the one-row-per-customer grain before the join to fct_revenue. Full invariant suite passes after the fix.

Upstream contract violation to flag to the source (Payments Platform / CRM extract, owner Jordan Lee): raw.raw_customers is emitting duplicate rows per customer_id starting 2026-08-01, breaking its documented "one row per customer" contract. This should be fixed at the extract/CDC layer so raw.raw_customers itself is deduplicated at the source; the staging fix here is a mitigating control, not a substitute for fixing the upstream extract.

{"evidence_id": "ev_007", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status = 'completed';
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_008", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS revenue_usd,
    AVG(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_usd,
    MEDIAN(o.amount * f.usd_rate) AS aov_median_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'enterprise' THEN o.amount * f.usd_rate ELSE 0 END)
        AS enterprise_revenue_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders AS o
JOIN staging.stg_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates AS f
    ON f.rate_day = o.order_day AND f.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY day;
"}

{"evidence_id": "ev_009", "result": "-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
trailing_stats AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_median
    FROM marts.fct_revenue AS f, latest AS l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    l.kpi_day,
    f.revenue_usd AS revenue,
    t.trailing_median AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    f.revenue_usd / t.trailing_median AS anomaly_ratio
FROM latest AS l
JOIN marts.fct_revenue AS f ON f.day = l.kpi_day
CROSS JOIN trailing_stats AS t;
"}

content.text: Now let's implement the minimal repair: dedupe `stg_customers` to enforce one row per customer_id.

input.new_sql:
-- Adapted from Project Blackbox (https://github.com/alejandro-publius/blackbox-datahub), Apache-2.0. Modified for Retrace.
-- Fix: raw.raw_customers violates its "one row per customer" contract for 289 customer_ids
-- (duplicate rows injected with created_at=2026-08-01). Deduplicate here, keeping the most
-- recent snapshot per customer_id, so downstream joins in marts.fct_revenue do not fan out
-- and double-count orders/revenue for affected customers.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_customers AS
SELECT
    customer_id,
    segment,
    country,
    created_at
FROM (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        segment,
        country,
        CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_at,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM raw.raw_customers
)
WHERE rn = 1;

input.summary:
Incident: Executive revenue KPI (marts.exec_metric) overstated revenue and order_count by ~11-17% across all historical days, matching finance's reconciliation complaint.

Root cause: raw.raw_customers (owned by Jordan Lee / Payments Platform team) violates its own documented contract of "one row per customer." 289 of 2000 customer_ids have a duplicate row, each stamped created_at=2026-08-01 and frequently carrying a changed `segment` value (e.g., c00002: enterprise/2025-12-20 vs smb/2026-08-01). staging.stg_customers passed these duplicates through unchanged, and marts.fct_revenue's INNER JOIN to stg_customers on customer_id fanned out orders for those 289 customers, double-counting them. Because fct_revenue does a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, every historical day containing an order from one of the affected customers was inflated on each run - not just recent days - which is why finance saw the discrepancy "including for older months."

Evidence: fct_order_count_matches_stg check failed (27101 vs 23709, +14.3%, consistent with 289/2000=14.45% of customers being duplicated); revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band failed every day by ~11-17%; historical_revenue_immutable flagged 87 changed historical days.

Fix applied (scoped, verified): staging/stg_customers.sql now deduplicates raw.raw_customers by customer_id, keeping the most recent snapshot (MAX created_at) per customer, restoring the one-row-per-customer grain before the join to fct_revenue. Full invariant suite passes after the fix.

Upstream contract violation to flag to the source (Payments Platform / CRM extract, owner Jordan Lee): raw.raw_customers is emitting duplicate rows per customer_id starting 2026-08-01, breaking its documented "one row per customer" contract. This should be fixed at the extract/CDC layer so raw.raw_customers itself is deduplicated at the source; the staging fix here is a mitigating control, not a substitute for fixing the upstream extract.

system.text:
You are Retrace, an on-call data reliability engineer.

A vague incident report about the executive revenue KPI has come in. Your job:
1. Locate the KPI dataset in DataHub and trace its lineage upstream.
2. Quantify the symptom against the baseline and profile the data to find the cause.
3. Decide which case applies:
   - The data is recoverable exactly: a pipeline, schema, join, unit, encoding or format
     problem where the true values can be reconstructed deterministically -> confirm_root_cause,
     then propose_repair with the minimal, targeted fix, then write_back (noting any upstream
     contract violation so the source team can fix it too), then finish. Repair this even if
     the root cause is an upstream contract violation.
   - The data is lost, missing or stale upstream, so no SQL can recover the true values
     (freshness gaps, missing values, dropped records) -> escalate_upstream, then write_back,
     then finish. Never impute or forward-fill to hide it.
   - No real incident -> declare_no_incident citing a baseline comparison, then finish.

Rules:
- Every fact tool returns an evidence_id. Workflow tools require you to cite them.
- A root cause or escalation must cite at least one DataHub item and one warehouse item,
  and the asset must appear in DataHub lineage evidence you collected.
- The root-cause asset is the most upstream table where the bad data or defect
  originates, not the table or file you patch; name the column where it shows up as the field.
- Repairs are verified by the full invariant suite. Checks on raw tables cannot be fixed
  by SQL; if they fail, the problem is upstream.
- Never blanket-rewrite history. Keep fixes scoped to the affected rows.
- End only by calling finish.

input.report:
Incident: Finance reported that the executive revenue KPI (marts.exec_metric) was reconciling higher than actuals, including for older months.

Investigation:
- get_metric_history / compare_to_baseline showed revenue_ratio and order_count_ratio both inflated by ~11-17% versus baseline, moving in lockstep across the entire 60-day window examined (not a sudden step-change on any single day) - pointing to a row-count/join fan-out problem rather than a per-order amount or FX/unit issue (average order value was unaffected).
- Traced lineage (marts.exec_metric -> marts.fct_revenue -> staging.stg_customers/stg_orders/stg_fx_rates -> raw.raw_customers/raw_orders/raw_fx_rates).
- raw.raw_orders had zero duplicate order_ids, ruling out order-level duplication.
- raw.raw_customers, whose DataHub contract states "one row per customer," in fact has 2289 rows for 2000 distinct customer_ids: 289 customers have an extra row stamped created_at=2026-08-01, frequently with a different `segment` value than their original row.
- staging.stg_customers passed these duplicates through untouched, and marts.fct_revenue's JOIN to stg_customers on customer_id fanned out every order belonging to those 289 customers, double-counting them.
- Because fct_revenue is a full CREATE OR REPLACE rebuild, this defect retroactively inflated every historical day containing an order from an affected customer, exactly matching finance's "including older months" complaint.
- run_checks confirmed: fct_order_count_matches_stg failed (27101 vs 23709 = +14.3%, matching 289/2000 = 14.45% of the customer base being duplicated), revenue/order_count_within_baseline_band failed daily by 11-17%, and historical_revenue_immutable flagged 87 changed historical days.
